title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 123
paragraphs: This was accomplished, and Cyrus, having received the hare from him, cut it open. Finding the paper within, he took it out and read it over. The writing said this: “Son of Cambyses, the gods watch over you, for otherwise you would never have come to so much good fortune. Take vengeance, then, on Astyages who is your murderer — for so far as his will is concerned, you are dead; but by the care of the gods and of me you are still alive. And this I think you have long ago learned from first to last, both how it happened concerning yourself and what I have suffered from Astyages, because I did not slay you but gave you to the herdsman. If, therefore, you will be guided by me, you shall be ruler of all the land over which Astyages now rules. Persuade the Persians to revolt, and march an army against the Medes. Whether I am appointed leader of the army against you, or whoever else of the Medes is in repute, you have what you desire; for these will be the first to attempt to destroy Astyages, revolting from him and coming over to your party. Consider, then, that here at least all is ready, and therefore do this, and do it with speed.”
